title: Remove All Occurrences of a Substring
statement:
You are given two strings, `s` and `part`. As long as `part` still appears in `s` as a contiguous block of characters, locate the copy of `part` that starts furthest to the left and delete it, joining the pieces on either side. Deleting a copy can bring characters together that form a new copy, which must then be removed too.

Return what remains of `s` once it no longer contains `part` (this may be the empty string).
constraints: s and part contain only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Doing exactly what the statement says (search for `part`, cut it out, search again from the start) is correct but can rescan the whole string after every removal. Notice that once a prefix of `s` has been cleaned, it never needs to be looked at again except at its very end: a new copy of `part` can only form where the cleaned prefix meets the next character. A stack holds that cleaned prefix, and only its top `m` characters ever need checking.

Removing a copy the moment it is completed is the same as removing the leftmost copy, because the cleaned stack itself contains no copy, so the leftmost copy in the whole string is the first one to be completed.

## Approach

1. Let `m` be the length of `part` and start with an empty `stack` of characters.
2. Push each character `ch` of `s` onto the stack.
3. If the stack has at least `m` characters, compare its top `m` characters with `part`.
4. If they all match, pop those `m` characters at once.
5. After the last character, join the stack into the answer.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "daabcbaabcbc"`, `part = "abc"`. Pushing `d a a b c` makes the top `abc`, so it is popped, leaving `da`. Pushing `b a a b c` gives `dabaabc`; the top `abc` is popped, leaving `daba`. Pushing `b` then `c` gives `dababc`; the top `abc` is popped again, leaving `dab`, which is the answer.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · m): each of the n pushes compares at most m characters.
- Space: O(n) for the stack.

## Pitfalls

- A removal can create a new copy that straddles the cut, as in `"ababcc"`; a single left-to-right scan that skips past each removal misses it.
- Only check once the stack holds at least `m` characters, or the index `stack.length - m` goes negative.
- Pop exactly `m` characters, not the whole stack; the characters below still matter.
- The answer can be the empty string, for example when `s` equals `part`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `m` | length of `part` |
| `stack` | the cleaned prefix, containing no copy of `part` |
| `ch` | the character of `s` being added |
| `matches` | whether the top `m` characters equal `part` |
| `j` | position inside `part` during the comparison |

narration.2: Remember the pattern length; only the top m characters of the stack can ever form a new copy.
narration.4: Read s once, left to right.
narration.5: Add the character to the cleaned prefix.
narration.6: With fewer than m characters on the stack, no copy of part can end here.
narration.10: Compare the top m characters of the stack with part, one position at a time.
narration.11: A single mismatch means the top is not a copy of part.
narration.16: The top m characters spell part...
narration.17: ...so delete them all at once; the characters below may now combine with the next ones.
narration.20: The stack holds everything that was never removed, in order.
